title: Meta’s Muse launch in Britain puts AI agents under UK regulatory spotlight
summary: Meta launches Muse in Britain, putting AI agents under UK regulatory spotlight
detailed: Meta launched its 'Muse' personal AI agent in the UK for users aged 18 and older on iOS, Android, WhatsApp, and the web, supported by local partners like Marks & Spencer and easyJet.
The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) warned tech firms that labeling as a technology provider does not exempt AI agents from financial regulations when executing regulated tasks.
Muse features safety guardrails preventing it from viewing passwords or payment details, sharing chats with advertisers, or sending emails/purchases without explicit user approval.
This regulatory warning matters because it establishes active oversight on personal AI agents performing financial activities like insurance renewals and payment processing.
sentences:
The warning came right after Meta announced the UK rollout of its Muse personal AI agent
Britain’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) warned tech firms that they must assess whether their AI agents provide regulated financial services including financial promotions, financial advice, or payment services and engage with regulators if they do.
According to the UK watchdog, labelling a business simply as a technology provider does not exempt it from financial regulations when its products execute regulated financial tasks.
The FCA advised consumers using AI agents to verify what protections apply if an issue occurs and they must evaluate what data they share, and ensure it is safe to do so.

While the FCA did not name specific companies, the warning comes after Meta's UK launch of its "Muse" personal AI agent which is capable of renewing car insurance, chasing refunds, and making online purchases.

On Tuesday, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg wrote on X, “Releasing Muse in the UK starting today -- now spells colour with a ‘u’.”
Muse automates everyday tasks such as sending emails, managing calendars, booking travel and Christmas shopping supported by UK partnerships with Marks & Spencer, Currys, Sainsbury’s, and easyJet.

To build user trust, Meta announces that Muse cannot see passwords or payment details, does not share chats with advertisers, requires explicit approval before making purchases or sending emails, and is monitored by a secondary "security agent."
Meta’s customizable AI assistant is available to people in the UK aged 18 and older via iOS and Android apps, inside WhatsApp and the muse.ai website.
